answer: Proof-of-Stake acts as a robust Sybil resistance mechanism where validator identity is tied to an economic anchor. To prevent malicious agents from creating fake identities to harbor voting power, the protocol requires a capital-intensive collateral lock. This creates a velvet constraint on network entry; attackers face prohibitive costs proportional to their stake, as acquiring sufficient assets to manipulate consensus triggers systemic devaluation of their own holdings, rendering the attack economically irrational.
